lot: Lot 6 - Multi-Client Process Ownership & Shared Observation

priority_mapping.0: P0 / Not parallel-safe — must run alone

assumptions: core = business logic; Rust API (Engine trait) = facade; CLI/TUI/WEB = thin clients. No client logic leaks into core.
Ownership state persists to disk at .macc/state/process_ownership.json using the atomic temp-file+rename pattern already established in MACC (crate::atomic_write). No new locking primitives needed.

ProcessOwnershipGuard and ProcessViewerGuard follow the CoordinatorPidGuard pattern (runtime.rs:250-299): constructor claims/registers, Drop() releases/unregisters. Callers store guards; Rust lifetimes enforce cleanup.
Ownership events are appended to the existing events.jsonl via append_coordinator_event_with_severity(). TUI (tick poll) and WEB (SSE) receive ownership events without any new transport layer.

tui/src/state.rs (4667 lines) is well above the 800-line anti-god-file threshold. All ownership logic goes into the new tui/src/ownership.rs companion file. state.rs additions are limited to field declarations and one-line delegation calls.
core/src/engine.rs (1787 lines) grows by ~80 lines of default-impl trait methods. This is acceptable given the existing pattern. All implementations delegate to core/src/service/process_ownership.rs.
core/src/lib.rs (2354 lines) receives only: one pub mod process_ownership; declaration. This is a single line addition.
The web frontend (web/src/) is built with React+TypeScript. Ownership UI uses existing component patterns (status badges, toast notifications) already present in the frontend.
ProcessKind enum covers: Coordinator, Supervisor, WebServer, TerminalSession. Performers are managed by the coordinator and not independently owned by clients.

First-connect-takes-ownership rule: if the ownership record has no owner and no pending takeover, the first caller to process_ownership_claim() becomes owner. Subsequent callers receive Viewer status.
Stale-client eviction: heartbeat TTL defaults to 60s (2x the 30s heartbeat interval). Eviction runs on every OwnershipStore::load() — lazy eviction, no background thread needed in core.

The web client identity is a per-browser-session UUID generated on first load and persisted in sessionStorage. The web server does not impersonate web clients; it registers a separate WebServer process identity for its own process.
L6-START-001 and L6-START-002 touch different process startup paths and can run in parallel after L6-ENG-001. L6-START-003 serializes before L6-WEB-002 because both touch cli/src/commands/web/mod.rs.
L6-TUI-002 (state.rs additions) serializes before L6-TUI-003 (render additions in lib.rs / ownership.rs) because the render references the new state fields.
All existing MACC functionality must continue to work — ownership is an additive layer. If the ownership store is missing or corrupt, all operations degrade gracefully to unowned mode.

tasks.title: Define process ownership domain types
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: No shared vocabulary exists for multi-client process ownership. All downstream tasks (store, events, engine, TUI, WEB) need a stable contract before implementation begins.
Key actions: Create core/src/process_ownership/mod.rs (module root with pub use re-exports). Create core/src/process_ownership/types.rs with: ClientKind enum (Tui, Web, Cli), ClientIdentity struct (client_id: String UUID, kind: ClientKind, connected_at: String ISO-8601), ProcessKind enum (Coordinator, Supervisor, WebServer, TerminalSession), ProcessHandle struct (kind: ProcessKind, project_root: PathBuf, pid: Option<i32>), OwnershipStatus enum (Owner, Viewer, Unregistered), OwnershipRecord struct (process: ProcessHandle, owner: Option<ClientIdentity>, viewers: Vec<ClientIdentity>, takeover_request: Option<TakeoverRequest>, started_at: String), TakeoverRequest struct (request_id: String, requester: ClientIdentity, requested_at: String). Add pub mod process_ownership; to core/src/lib.rs. All types derive Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq.
Out of scope: Store implementation, events, Engine trait, any behavior.
Success criteria: core/src/process_ownership/types.rs compiles with all types, derives, and no dead-code warnings. lib.rs declares the module. No logic, only types.
tasks.objective: Establish the shared vocabulary for multi-client ownership that all other L6 tasks depend on.
tasks.result: core/src/process_ownership/mod.rs and core/src/process_ownership/types.rs exist and compile. core/src/lib.rs declares pub mod process_ownership.
steps: Create core/src/process_ownership/ directory.
Create types.rs with ClientKind, ClientIdentity, ProcessKind, ProcessHandle, OwnershipStatus, OwnershipRecord, TakeoverRequest structs/enums.
Create mod.rs re-exporting all public types from types.rs.
Add pub mod process_ownership; to core/src/lib.rs.
Run cargo check — no errors, no dead-code warnings on types.
tasks.notes: Contracts-first task. Keep it pure — no behavior, no file I/O, no events. ProcessHandle.pid is Option<i32> because the handle can be constructed before a process has a PID (e.g., during startup before execve). client_id is a String (UUID v4) so it can be generated without pulling in uuid crate if not already present — use format!("{:x}", rand_u128) or existing uuid dependency.

tasks.title: Implement OwnershipStore: file-backed process ownership persistence
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: Ownership state must survive process restarts and be visible across CLI, TUI, and WEB processes without in-process shared memory.
Key actions: Create core/src/process_ownership/store.rs. OwnershipStore holds an in-memory Vec<OwnershipRecord>. File path: {project_root}/.macc/state/process_ownership.json. Methods: load(repo_root) -> Result<OwnershipStore> (reads and deserializes file, creates empty store if file missing, runs lazy stale-eviction on load), save(&self, repo_root) -> Result<()> (serializes to temp file + renames atomically, following existing crate::atomic_write pattern), get_record(handle) -> Option<&OwnershipRecord>, upsert_record(record), remove_record(handle). load_and_modify(repo_root, fn(store) -> Result<T>) -> Result<T> helper: loads, applies closure, saves atomically — callers use this to avoid TOCTOU. Update mod.rs to pub use store::OwnershipStore.
Out of scope: Claim/release/viewer logic (service layer, L6-OWN-005). Events. Heartbeat eviction details (L6-OWN-004).
Success criteria: OwnershipStore can round-trip a full OwnershipRecord to/from JSON. load() returns empty store when file does not exist. save() is atomic (uses temp+rename). load_and_modify() serializes concurrent modifications correctly in unit tests.
tasks.objective: Provide a reliable, atomic, file-backed store for process ownership state shared across all MACC client processes.
tasks.result: core/src/process_ownership/store.rs compiles with OwnershipStore, round-trip unit tests pass, atomic write verified.
steps: Create store.rs with OwnershipStore struct holding Vec<OwnershipRecord>.
Implement load(): read JSON from .macc/state/process_ownership.json; return empty store on NotFound; surface other IO errors as MaccError::Io.
Implement save(): serialize to serde_json::to_string_pretty, write to .macc/state/process_ownership.json.tmp, rename to final path — matching existing atomic_write pattern.
Implement get_record(), upsert_record(), remove_record() helper methods.
Implement load_and_modify() convenience wrapper.
Write unit tests: empty file round-trip, record upsert/remove, atomic write (verify temp file is gone after save).
Update mod.rs to pub use store::OwnershipStore.
tasks.notes: Do not use crate::atomic_write directly — that function expects a ProjectPaths reference. Mirror the pattern (temp path = final path + '.tmp', rename). Stale-eviction is called from load() via the heartbeat module (L6-OWN-004); use a no-op stub for now with a TODO comment so this task can be parallel with L6-OWN-004.

tasks.title: Implement OwnershipEventBroadcaster: emit ownership events to events.jsonl
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: TUI (tick poll) and WEB (SSE) already consume events.jsonl for coordinator status. Ownership events must flow through the same transport so clients receive ownership state changes without a new notification channel.
Key actions: Create core/src/process_ownership/events.rs. Define OwnershipEventBroadcaster with a single method: emit(repo_root, event_type, handle, payload_fields) -> () (infallible — ownership events are best-effort, never block the caller). Internally calls append_coordinator_event_with_severity with task_id="-", phase="ownership", severity="info". Implement a helper for each event type as free functions: emit_ownership_claimed, emit_ownership_released, emit_viewer_joined, emit_viewer_left, emit_takeover_requested, emit_takeover_accepted, emit_takeover_rejected, emit_owner_stale. Each function encodes the ClientIdentity and ProcessHandle into the message string as structured JSON. Update mod.rs to pub use events::*.
Out of scope: New transport mechanism. Changing events.jsonl schema. Any reads from events.jsonl.
Success criteria: emit_ownership_claimed() appends a valid JSON line to events.jsonl. All helper functions compile. Calling emit on a repo with no events.jsonl creates it (follows existing append behavior).
tasks.objective: Pipe ownership state-change notifications through events.jsonl so existing TUI poll and WEB SSE consumers receive them without new infrastructure.
tasks.result: core/src/process_ownership/events.rs with OwnershipEventBroadcaster and typed helper functions. Events appear in events.jsonl when called.
steps: Create events.rs, import append_coordinator_event_with_severity from crate::coordinator::helpers.
Implement emit() as the base method: maps handle+payload to the append call.
Implement typed helper functions (emit_ownership_claimed etc.) each calling emit() with the correct event_type string and a JSON payload including client_id, process_kind, pid.
All emit functions are infallible (return ()) — log warnings internally on failure but do not propagate errors.
Write a unit test that calls emit_ownership_claimed on a temp repo and verifies the resulting events.jsonl line is valid JSON with expected fields.
Update mod.rs to re-export helper functions.
tasks.notes: Event type strings must be stable: 'ownership_claimed', 'ownership_released', 'viewer_joined', 'viewer_left', 'takeover_requested', 'takeover_accepted', 'takeover_rejected', 'owner_stale'. These will be parsed by TUI and WEB. Keep them lowercase_snake_case matching existing coordinator event_type conventions.

tasks.title: Implement stale-client heartbeat eviction
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: A client that disconnects without cleanup leaves a stale ownership or viewer entry that blocks other clients from claiming ownership. Lazy eviction on store load keeps the store clean without background threads.
Key actions: Create core/src/process_ownership/heartbeat.rs. Define HeartbeatConfig { ttl_seconds: u64 } with default 60s. Implement evict_stale_clients(store: &mut OwnershipStore, config: &HeartbeatConfig) which: for each OwnershipRecord, removes viewer entries whose connected_at (parsed as ISO-8601) is older than ttl_seconds from now; if the owner entry is stale, clears owner, emits emit_owner_stale, promotes oldest non-stale viewer to owner if any viewer exists. Call evict_stale_clients from OwnershipStore::load() before returning (replace the TODO stub from L6-OWN-002). Update mod.rs. Update OwnershipRecord.owner/viewers entries to carry last_heartbeat: String ISO-8601 in addition to connected_at — heartbeat updates this field. Update types.rs accordingly (ClientIdentity gains last_heartbeat: String).
Out of scope: Background eviction loop. Changing heartbeat send logic (service layer).
Success criteria: evict_stale_clients() removes entries with last_heartbeat older than ttl_seconds. Stale owner triggers emit_owner_stale and promotes a viewer. Unit tests cover: all-fresh (no eviction), stale-viewer-removed, stale-owner-promotes-viewer, stale-owner-no-viewers-clears-owner.
tasks.objective: Prevent stale client entries from blocking ownership claims by lazily evicting them whenever the store is loaded.
tasks.result: core/src/process_ownership/heartbeat.rs with evict_stale_clients(). OwnershipStore::load() calls it. Unit tests pass.
steps: Add last_heartbeat: String field to ClientIdentity in types.rs.
Create heartbeat.rs with HeartbeatConfig and evict_stale_clients().
Parse last_heartbeat as chrono::DateTime<Utc>; compare to Utc::now() - Duration::seconds(config.ttl_seconds).
For stale owner: clear owner field, emit emit_owner_stale, find oldest-by-connected_at non-stale viewer, promote to owner, remove from viewers list.
Wire evict_stale_clients into OwnershipStore::load() replacing the TODO stub.
Write unit tests: fresh entries untouched, stale viewer removed, stale owner promotes viewer.
Update mod.rs re-exports.
tasks.notes: ClientIdentity.last_heartbeat is set equal to connected_at on creation, then updated by process_heartbeat() in the service layer (L6-OWN-005). Use chrono (already a MACC dependency) for timestamp parsing and comparison.

tasks.title: Implement process ownership service layer and guard types
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The Engine trait and process startup hooks need a well-defined service API for all ownership operations. The guard pattern (RAII) ensures cleanup on process exit matches the established CoordinatorPidGuard pattern.
Key actions: Create core/src/service/process_ownership.rs with the following functions, all taking repo_root: &Path: claim_owner(repo_root, handle, identity) -> Result<OwnershipStatus> — loads store via load_and_modify, first-connect-takes-ownership rule: if no owner present, set identity as owner, emit_ownership_claimed, return Owner; if caller is already owner, return Owner; else register as viewer, emit_viewer_joined, return Viewer. release_owner(repo_root, handle, client_id) -> Result<()> — removes owner entry, emits emit_ownership_released. register_viewer(repo_root, handle, identity) -> Result<()> — adds viewer if not already present, emits emit_viewer_joined. unregister_viewer(repo_root, handle, client_id) -> Result<()> — removes viewer entry, emits emit_viewer_left. request_takeover(repo_root, handle, requester) -> Result<String> — sets takeover_request field, emits emit_takeover_requested, returns request_id UUID. respond_takeover(repo_root, handle, owner_client_id, request_id, accept: bool) -> Result<()> — validates owner_client_id is current owner, clears takeover_request, if accepted: transfers owner to requester + emits emit_takeover_accepted; if rejected: emits emit_takeover_rejected. heartbeat(repo_root, handle, client_id) -> Result<()> — updates last_heartbeat on matching owner or viewer entry. get_record(repo_root, handle) -> Result<Option<OwnershipRecord>>. list_records(repo_root) -> Result<Vec<OwnershipRecord>>. Define ProcessOwnershipGuard { repo_root, handle, client_id } with Drop calling release_owner(). Define ProcessViewerGuard { repo_root, handle, client_id } with Drop calling unregister_viewer().
Out of scope: Engine trait wiring (L6-ENG-001). Process startup hooks (L6-START-*).
Success criteria: All service functions compile. ProcessOwnershipGuard::drop() calls release_owner(). ProcessViewerGuard::drop() calls unregister_viewer(). Unit tests: claim by first client returns Owner, claim by second client returns Viewer, takeover accepted transfers owner, takeover rejected keeps original owner.
tasks.objective: Provide the complete service API for ownership operations, with guard types that enforce cleanup via Rust drop semantics.
tasks.result: core/src/service/process_ownership.rs with all service functions, ProcessOwnershipGuard, ProcessViewerGuard. Unit tests pass.
steps: Create core/src/service/process_ownership.rs.
Implement claim_owner() with first-connect-takes-ownership logic.
Implement release_owner(), register_viewer(), unregister_viewer(), request_takeover(), respond_takeover(), heartbeat(), get_record(), list_records().
Define ProcessOwnershipGuard struct; implement Drop calling release_owner() (infallible in Drop — log on error).
Define ProcessViewerGuard struct; implement Drop calling unregister_viewer() (infallible in Drop).
Add pub mod process_ownership; to core/src/service/mod.rs (or equivalent registration point).
Write unit tests covering first-connect-takes-ownership, second-client-becomes-viewer, takeover-accepted, takeover-rejected.
tasks.notes: All load_and_modify calls are the serialization point for concurrent store access. claim_owner() must generate a fresh last_heartbeat = now() for the new identity entry. ProcessOwnershipGuard and ProcessViewerGuard are the primary API for callers — direct service function calls are for edge cases (CLI recovery, tests).

tasks.title: Add process ownership methods to the Engine trait
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: TUI, WEB, and CLI are clients of the Engine trait. All ownership operations must be accessible through the same facade pattern used for coordinator operations, without clients importing service internals directly.
Key actions: Add the following default-impl methods to the Engine trait in core/src/engine.rs, each delegating to core::service::process_ownership::
  process_ownership_claim(&self, repo_root, handle, identity) -> Result<(OwnershipStatus, ProcessOwnershipGuard)> — calls service::process_ownership::claim_owner(), returns status + guard.
  process_ownership_release(&self, repo_root, handle, client_id) — calls release_owner().
  process_ownership_status(&self, repo_root, handle) -> Result<Option<OwnershipRecord>> — calls get_record().
  process_ownership_request_takeover(&self, repo_root, handle, requester) -> Result<String> — calls request_takeover().
  process_ownership_respond_takeover(&self, repo_root, handle, owner_client_id, request_id, accept) -> Result<()>.
  process_register_viewer(&self, repo_root, handle, identity) -> Result<ProcessViewerGuard> — calls register_viewer() + constructs guard.
  process_heartbeat(&self, repo_root, handle, client_id) -> Result<()> — calls heartbeat().
  process_list_running(&self, repo_root) -> Result<Vec<OwnershipRecord>> — calls list_records().
All are default implementations; no override needed in MaccEngine.
Out of scope: Changing any existing Engine method. Modifying any coordinator, worktree, or config methods.
Success criteria: All new methods are present in the trait with default implementations. cargo check passes. Calling engine.process_ownership_claim() from a test compiles and returns the expected result.
tasks.objective: Expose the complete process ownership API through the Engine facade so CLI/TUI/WEB access it uniformly without importing service internals.
tasks.result: core/src/engine.rs has 8 new default-impl ownership methods. Existing tests unaffected. cargo check passes.
steps: Add use crate::process_ownership::{OwnershipRecord, OwnershipStatus, ProcessHandle, ClientIdentity}; and use crate::service::process_ownership::{ProcessOwnershipGuard, ProcessViewerGuard}; to engine.rs imports.
Add process_ownership_claim() default impl calling service::process_ownership::claim_owner().
Add process_register_viewer() returning ProcessViewerGuard directly.
Add remaining 6 methods (release, status, request_takeover, respond_takeover, heartbeat, list_running) as default impls.
Verify cargo check passes with no new warnings on the trait definition.
Write a smoke test: create a temp repo, call engine.process_ownership_claim() twice with different identities, verify first is Owner and second is Viewer.
tasks.notes: Engine trait is 1787 lines. Add the new methods in a clearly delimited section with a // --- Process Ownership --- comment header, following the existing section-comment pattern. The methods return ProcessOwnershipGuard / ProcessViewerGuard so callers hold them — the guard's Drop handles release. MaccEngine (the concrete type) gets these methods for free via the default impl.

tasks.title: Wire coordinator startup auto-claim and exit ownership release
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: When the coordinator subprocess starts, it should atomically claim ownership of its process handle so TUI and WEB clients see it as owned and can register as viewers.
Key actions: In core/src/coordinator/runtime.rs, add a ProcessOwnershipGuard field to CoordinatorRunState alongside the existing coordinator_pid_guard: Option<CoordinatorPidGuard>. In ensure_performer_ipc_listener() (or the coordinator startup path that already creates CoordinatorPidGuard::new()), after the PidGuard is created: construct ProcessHandle { kind: ProcessKind::Coordinator, project_root: repo_root.to_path_buf(), pid: Some(process::id() as i32) }, call service::process_ownership::claim_owner(repo_root, handle, identity) with a Cli identity (the coordinator subprocess is launched by the CLI), store the resulting ProcessOwnershipGuard in CoordinatorRunState. The guard's Drop releases ownership when the coordinator exits. Generate the client_id as format!("coordinator-{}", std::process::id()).
Out of scope: Handling takeover requests inside the coordinator loop (that is a TUI concern). Viewer registration (done by TUI/WEB clients after connecting).
Success criteria: After coordinator startup, .macc/state/process_ownership.json contains an entry for ProcessKind::Coordinator with an owner entry. On coordinator exit, the owner entry is cleared (guard Drop fires). Unit test: start coordinator (mocked), verify record exists; drop state, verify record cleared.
tasks.objective: Make the coordinator atomically claim process ownership on startup so clients can discover and observe it.
tasks.result: CoordinatorRunState holds Option<ProcessOwnershipGuard>. Coordinator startup writes ownership record. Coordinator exit clears it.
steps: Add ownership_guard: Option<ProcessOwnershipGuard> to CoordinatorRunState in runtime.rs.
After CoordinatorPidGuard::new() succeeds, construct ProcessHandle for Coordinator kind.
Call service::process_ownership::claim_owner() and store the returned guard in state.ownership_guard.
Log ownership_claimed event on success (the broadcaster handles this internally).
Verify the guard's Drop fires by writing a unit test that drops CoordinatorRunState and checks the store is cleared.
tasks.notes: The coordinator subprocess is a CLI-spawned process, so its client_identity.kind = ClientKind::Cli. This is correct — the process itself is not a TUI or WEB client. TUI will register as viewer (L6-TUI-002) after connecting. Do not panic if claim_owner fails (e.g., previous stale entry) — log warning and continue.

tasks.title: Wire web server startup auto-claim and add ownership routes to web router
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The web server is a long-running process. On startup it should claim ProcessKind::WebServer ownership, and the router must expose all ownership API endpoints so WEB clients can register, query, and request takeover.
Key actions: (A) Startup hook — in cli/src/commands/web/mod.rs, WebState gains ownership_guard: Option<Arc<ProcessOwnershipGuard>> (Arc because WebState is Clone + shared across Axum handlers). In WebCommand::run(), after binding the listener: construct ProcessHandle { kind: ProcessKind::WebServer, project_root: paths.root, pid: Some(process::id() as i32) }, call engine.process_ownership_claim() via state.engine, store guard in state.ownership_guard. On server shutdown the Arc drops and releases ownership. (B) Routes — add new ownership routes to build_web_router(): GET /api/v1/processes, GET /api/v1/processes/:handle/ownership, POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/claim, POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/release, POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/viewer, DELETE /api/v1/processes/:handle/viewer, POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/takeover/request, POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/takeover/respond, POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/heartbeat — all routed to handlers in cli/src/commands/web/ownership.rs (L6-WEB-001).
Out of scope: Implementing the handler bodies (L6-WEB-001). Frontend (L6-WEB-003).
Success criteria: build_web_router() compiles with all new routes. WebState holds ownership_guard. Server startup writes WebServer ownership record. cargo check passes.
tasks.objective: Ensure the web server claims its process ownership on startup and the API surface for ownership operations is declared in the router.

tasks.title: Add ownership lifecycle to AppState: fields, startup registration, tick heartbeat, exit cleanup
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: AppState must hold the TUI's client identity, track its ownership/viewer status for running processes, send periodic heartbeats, and clean up on exit. All additions to state.rs must be minimal, delegating to tui/src/ownership.rs and the Engine trait.
Key actions: In tui/src/state.rs: (1) Add fields: client_identity: ClientIdentity (generated in new() as UUID+TUI kind), ownership_state: TuiOwnershipState, ownership_guard: Option<ProcessOwnershipGuard>, viewer_guards: Vec<ProcessViewerGuard>. (2) In new(): generate client_identity; call scan_and_register_as_viewer() (defined below). (3) Add scan_and_register_as_viewer(&mut self): calls engine.process_list_running() for project_paths, for each running process calls engine.process_register_viewer(), stores ProcessViewerGuard in viewer_guards; sets ownership_state.record. (4) In start_managed_coordinator_command(): before spawning, call engine.process_ownership_claim(); if result is Owner, store ProcessOwnershipGuard in self.ownership_guard; if Viewer, the guard from process_register_viewer is already stored. (5) In tick(): every 5 seconds (use a last_ownership_refresh Instant), refresh ownership records by calling engine.process_ownership_status() and update ownership_state; check ownership_state.pending_incoming_request for new takeover requests; call engine.process_heartbeat() for each held guard. (6) In the TUI exit path (load_config cleanup or on TerminalGuard drop signal): drop ownership_guard and viewer_guards explicitly before exit. tasks.title: Implement web ownership API handlers
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: WEB clients need REST endpoints to register as viewers, query ownership, request takeover, and respond. Handlers follow the existing ApiError/WebState pattern.
Key actions: Create cli/src/commands/web/ownership.rs. Implement Axum handlers for each route declared in L6-START-003: get_processes_handler (GET /api/v1/processes) — calls engine.process_list_running() → Vec<ApiOwnershipRecord>. get_ownership_handler (GET /api/v1/processes/:handle/ownership) — deserializes ProcessHandle from path, calls engine.process_ownership_status(). post_claim_handler (POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/claim) — body: ClientIdentity JSON, calls engine.process_ownership_claim() → ApiOwnershipResult. post_release_handler (POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/release) — body: { client_id }, calls engine.process_ownership_release(). post_register_viewer_handler (POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/viewer) — body: ClientIdentity, calls engine.process_register_viewer(). delete_unregister_viewer_handler (DELETE /api/v1/processes/:handle/viewer) — body: { client_id }. post_takeover_request_handler (POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/takeover/request). post_takeover_respond_handler (POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/takeover/respond) — body: { owner_client_id, request_id, accept: bool }. post_heartbeat_handler (POST /api/v1/processes/:handle/heartbeat) — body: { client_id }. Define ApiOwnershipRecord, ApiOwnershipResult serializable response types mirroring OwnershipRecord but with camelCase field names. ProcessHandle path param deserialization: encode handle as URL-safe base64 of JSON-serialized ProcessHandle OR use a flat query param encoding (kind + project_root + pid). Choose the simpler approach — query params are fine: GET /api/v1/processes?kind=Coordinator.
Out of scope: Frontend (L6-WEB-003). Route registration (L6-START-003).
Success criteria: All handlers compile against WebState. Unit tests (existing web tests pattern in cli/src/commands/web/tests.rs) cover: list processes (empty), claim (first caller = owner), register viewer, heartbeat. HTTP 404 on unknown handle, 409 on double-claim attempt that returns Viewer.

tasks.title: Wire web server heartbeat loop and web client identity persistence
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: WEB clients (browser tabs) need a persistent identity and a mechanism to keep their viewer/ownership entries alive. The web server should send heartbeats on behalf of connected web client sessions.
Key actions: (A) Browser-side client identity — in the frontend's API layer (web/src/api/ or equivalent), on first app load generate a UUID (crypto.randomUUID()) and persist it to sessionStorage as macc_client_id. Include this client_id in every ownership API request body. Register beforeunload handler to call DELETE /api/v1/processes/:handle/viewer. (B) Server-side heartbeat proxy — add a background task in the Axum server (tokio::spawn in WebCommand::run() after server is started) that every 30s calls engine.process_heartbeat() for each active process × each web client that has registered a viewer via the ownership store. (C) On SSE events_handler: when a new SSE connection is established, call engine.process_register_viewer() with a Web client identity whose client_id is taken from a query param or header (?client_id=UUID). Return the viewer guard as part of the SSE stream context (drop it when the stream ends — SSE disconnection auto-releases).
Out of scope: Frontend UI components (L6-WEB-003).
Success criteria: SSE connection registers web client as viewer. SSE disconnect triggers unregister_viewer (guard drop). Server heartbeat loop updates last_heartbeat in ownership store. Client identity persists in sessionStorage.

tasks.title: Unit tests for OwnershipStore concurrent safety and stale eviction
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The OwnershipStore is the single shared state file for all client processes. Correctness under concurrent load_and_modify() calls and correctness of stale eviction are critical to the ownership feature's reliability.
Key actions: In core/src/process_ownership/store.rs (or a dedicated tests module), add: (1) Concurrent write test: spawn 10 threads each calling load_and_modify() on the same temp repo path with different claims; verify final state is consistent (exactly one owner per record, no duplicate entries). (2) Stale eviction test: create a store with an owner entry whose last_heartbeat is 120s in the past; call load(); verify the owner is evicted and ownership_guard is None. (3) Stale viewer eviction test: create a store with 3 viewers — 2 stale, 1 fresh; call load(); verify 2 stale viewers removed, 1 remains. (4) Stale owner promotes viewer test: create store with stale owner + 1 fresh viewer; call load(); verify viewer is promoted to owner. (5) Round-trip test: serialize + deserialize OwnershipRecord with all fields populated; verify equality.
Out of scope: TUI or WEB integration. Network behavior.
Success criteria: All 5 test cases pass. cargo test on core crate passes including new tests. No data races (test with --test-threads=1 if needed for fs tests).
tasks.objective: Verify OwnershipStore correctness under concurrent access and validate the stale-eviction logic that underpins the first-connect-takes-ownership rule.
tasks.result: 5 new unit tests in store.rs or process_ownership tests module. All pass. No regressions in existing core tests.

tasks.notes: Use tempfile::TempDir for isolation. For concurrent tests, use a Mutex<()> or file-system locks if needed — the load_and_modify pattern serializes writes but multiple threads may still race on the outer load. Fabricate stale timestamps using chrono::Utc::now() - Duration::seconds(120).to_rfc3339() for last_heartbeat.

tasks.title: check lot 6
tasks.description: Problem/Goal: The complete implementation of batch 6 'prd_l6.json' needs to be verified : The objective of this prd is to edit MACC to give the possibility of having TUI or WEB clients accessing the same process (for exemple 'macc coordinator') instance at the same time. - The goal is to make the web, TUI clients simple viewers, allowing them to view and modify configurations all process and command. - The TUI is the reference, as it is currently the most functional and complete. - However, if one client launches a process, the others are simply viewers if the client that launched it is still connected. Therefore, only one client can modify the process, and the others are viewers. A client can request and take control, and the other can accept or reject the request. - Even if no client is connected, the processes continue. The first client to connect takes control, not only viewing the processes but also having the right to modify them. Subsequent clients will be mere viewers. - And this is true for all processes in MACC, not just

. - Note that the architecture is of the type: core = business logic, Rust API = facade, CLI/TUI/WEB = clients: 1. It must be tool-agnostic! Use adapters if needed. 2. Scalable 3. Factored as much as possible 4. Modular
